155	
156	### Branch model overview
157	
158	```
159	main
160	 └── release/v*.*.*       ← release candidates, gates UAT + PROD
161	      └── develop          ← integration baseline, gates Dev + SIT
162	           └── feature/*   ← feature work, runs locally only (no MRT deployment)
163	hotfix/*                   ← branches from main, merges back to main + develop
164	```
165	
166	### Branch definitions and rules
167	
168	#### `main`
169	- Represents production. Always deployable.
170	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR from `release/v*.*.*` only.
171	- Required status checks: `Digital SIT Gate`, `UAT ✓` (manual), post-canary smoke.
172	- Tag every merge: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` — e.g. `v1.3.0`.
173	- Triggers: production deployment pipeline (manual approval gate).
174	
175	#### `release/v*.*.*`
176	- Naming convention: `release/v1.3.0`, `release/v1.3.1` etc.
177	- Branched from `develop` when a release window is scheduled.
178	- No new features merged here — bug fixes and release-prep only.
179	- Required status checks on PR to `main`: `Digital SIT Gate` (run against release branch),
180	  `UAT ✓`.
181	- Triggers: STAGE deployment pipeline (manual trigger after Jira booking approved).
182	- Git tag on branch creation: `release/digital/v1.3.0` — referenced in Jira booking ticket.
183	
184	#### `develop`
185	- Integration baseline. All feature branches merge here.
186	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR with minimum 1 approval.
187	- Required status checks on PR merge: lint, unit tests, bundle size, security scan.
188	- Triggers on merge:
189	  - Auto-deploy to MRT staging (Dev tier)
190	  - Auto-push to MRT sit (SIT tier) — fires after `sit-gate` passes
191	- Git tag convention on significant milestones: `develop/{sprint}/{date}` — e.g.
192	  `develop/sprint-12/2026-05-09`. Used to anchor SIT bundle reference for NewStore.
193	
194	#### `feature/*`
195	- Naming convention: `feature/JIRA-123_short-description`
196	- Branched from `develop`. Merges back to `develop` via PR.
197	- Runs locally only (`npm start`). No MRT deployment for feature branches.
198	- No required status checks beyond lint and unit tests — this tier is for fast iteration.
199	- Delete branch on merge.
200	
201	#### `hotfix/*`
202	- Naming convention: `hotfix/JIRA-456_short-description`
203	- Branched from `main` only. Never from `develop`.
204	- Merges to `main` first, then back-merged to `develop`.
205	- Abbreviated pipeline: skips load test, keeps smoke test and approval gate.
206	- Do not skip the production approval gate under any circumstances.
207	- Tag: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch+1}` — e.g. `v1.3.1`.

2	
3	**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.
4	
5	See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.
6	
7	## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)
8	
9	To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
10	- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
11	- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
12	- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.
13	
14	## Release Branch Behaviour
15	
16	When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.
17	
18	**Before writing any code, always:**
19	1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
20	2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
21	3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.
22	
23	**Allowed on release branches:**
24	- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
25	- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
26	- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch
27	
28	**Not allowed on release branches:**
29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
30	- Refactoring
31	- Dependency changes
32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
33	
34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
35	
36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
37	
38	```bash
39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
42	
43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
45	```
46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

7	## Pre-Build Decisions

9	These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

20	### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
21	
22	**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
23	**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.
24	
25	### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
26	
27	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
28	**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.
29	
30	### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
31	
32	**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
33	**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
34	**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
35	**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
36	**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
37	**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.

110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111	
112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

114	## Overrides Pattern
115	
116	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
117	
118	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
119	
120	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
121	
122	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
123	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
124	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
125	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

160	## Contentful Content Type Management
161	
162	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.
163	
164	**Key paths:**
165	
166	- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
167	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)
168	
169	**To register a new content type:**
170	
171	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
172	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
173	
174	**To run the sync:**
175	
176	```
177	npm run sync:contentful
178	```
179	
180	Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account — in `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold it, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running the sync). Get the token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
181	
182	The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).
183	
184	**Relationship to the React component:**
185	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
186	
187	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

204	## Integration Map
205	
206	All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.
207	
208	**Boundary key:**
209	
210	- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
211	- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
212	- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
213	- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
214	- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
215	- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
216	- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

249	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
250	
251	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

253	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
254	
255	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

257	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
258	
259	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
260	
261	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
262	
263	```ts
264	import { Pool } from 'undici';
265	
266	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
267	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
268	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
269	  timeout: 8000,
270	});
271	
272	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
273	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
274	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
275	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
276	  });
277	}
278	```

# Environment Strategy, Branching & SIT Pipeline — Claude Code Briefing

## Programme Context

Zimmermann is migrating from Magento 2 to Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) using the PWA Kit
(`template-retail-react-app`) as the storefront baseline, deployed on Managed Runtime (MRT).

Seven storefronts are in scope: AU, UK, US domestic, US international (Global-e), EU domestic,
EU international (Global-e), and ME. The Digital pipeline must support all six active SFCC
storefronts simultaneously. NewStore (OMS) runs a parallel SIT cycle on its own cadence and
converges with Digital only at the STAGE tier.

Zimmermann has 20 SFCC sandboxes available and no MRT environment licence restriction.
This enables a clean six-tier topology with no shared-environment contention.

164	```
165	
166	### Branch definitions and rules
167	
168	#### `main`
169	- Represents production. Always deployable.
170	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR from `release/v*.*.*` only.
171	- Required status checks: `Digital SIT Gate`, `UAT ✓` (manual), post-canary smoke.
172	- Tag every merge: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` — e.g. `v1.3.0`.
173	- Triggers: production deployment pipeline (manual approval gate).
174	
175	#### `release/v*.*.*`
176	- Naming convention: `release/v1.3.0`, `release/v1.3.1` etc.
177	- Branched from `develop` when a release window is scheduled.
178	- No new features merged here — bug fixes and release-prep only.
179	- Required status checks on PR to `main`: `Digital SIT Gate` (run against release branch),
180	  `UAT ✓`.
181	- Triggers: STAGE deployment pipeline (manual trigger after Jira booking approved).
182	- Git tag on branch creation: `release/digital/v1.3.0` — referenced in Jira booking ticket.
183	
184	#### `develop`
185	- Integration baseline. All feature branches merge here.
186	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR with minimum 1 approval.
187	- Required status checks on PR merge: lint, unit tests, bundle size, security scan.
188	- Triggers on merge:
189	  - Auto-deploy to MRT staging (Dev tier)
190	  - Auto-push to MRT sit (SIT tier) — fires after `sit-gate` passes
191	- Git tag convention on significant milestones: `develop/{sprint}/{date}` — e.g.
192	  `develop/sprint-12/2026-05-09`. Used to anchor SIT bundle reference for NewStore.
193

195	- Naming convention: `feature/JIRA-123_short-description`
196	- Branched from `develop`. Merges back to `develop` via PR.
197	- Runs locally only (`npm start`). No MRT deployment for feature branches.
198	- No required status checks beyond lint and unit tests — this tier is for fast iteration.
199	- Delete branch on merge.
200	
201	#### `hotfix/*`
202	- Naming convention: `hotfix/JIRA-456_short-description`

I'm investigating whether this repo (zimmermann-pwa, a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront) actually needs a `release/*` branch type in its GitFlow, or whether that's unused ceremony. AGENTS.md already documents an elaborate `release/*` / `hotfix/*` / `fix/release-*` branching policy (see the Branch Rules table and the "Tier 1 Approval" section), but I need to know whether that policy reflects real, exercised practice versus being aspirational/unused. Gather evidence, do NOT make any judgment calls or write any code — just report facts with file:line citations.

Please investigate and report back on each of these (be thorough, this feeds a real architectural decision):

1. **Git history**: Run `git branch -a` and `git log --all --oneline --grep="release" -i` and `git log --all --decorate --oneline | grep -i release` and `git tag -l`. Has a `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branch ever actually existed in this repo's history (local or remote-tracking refs)? Any merge commits referencing release branches? Check `git log --all --merges --oneline` for "Merge pull request" messages mentioning release/hotfix.

2. **`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`**: Read this file in full and summarize what it prescribes (plan-first rules, fix/release-* sub-branch flow, GitFlow back-merge rules). Note whether it reads as fully fleshed out or as a stub/placeholder.

3. **CI/CD workflows**: Read every file in `.github/workflows/`. For each, note: does it have conditional logic keyed on `release/**` (e.g. BrowserStack full suite only on release, SIT gate only on release, `.browserstack.yml` scoping)? Is there a separate deploy workflow for staging vs production, and does it key off branch name (release/main) or something else (tags, manual dispatch, MRT environment)? Quote the relevant branch-matching conditions.

4. **Managed Runtime deploy model**: Check `package.json` scripts (the `push` script), `mobify.config.js`, and any deploy-related docs in `.docs/` (e.g. architecture.md's deployment section) to understand how `npm run push` actually promotes code to Managed Runtime environments (dev/staging/production bundles). Does deployment appear to be tag-based, branch-based, or manual-bundle-based? Does it need a long-lived release branch, or does MRT's bundle/environment model make that unnecessary?

5. **`.docs/architecture.md`**: Read it and summarize anything about branching strategy, release cadence, or deployment pipeline.

6. **`.docs/memory/projectState.md`** and any other files under `.docs/memory/`: read them for anything about current release cadence, sprint cutover process, or whether a release branch has been discussed/decided.

7. **package.json**: check the `version` field and whether there's any semantic-release / changelog-automation config tied to a release branch.

8. **`.claude/skills/generate-changelog/`**: read the SKILL.md — it's described as "Generate a release changelog... Use before cutting a release branch." Does its content assume release branches are a real, active mechanism, or does it read as forward-looking/unused?

9. Search the whole repo (grep, not just docs) for "release/" branch references outside AGENTS.md/rules files — e.g. in README, CONTRIBUTING, workflow YAML comments — to see how pervasively the concept is wired in vs. just declared in policy docs.

Report back concisely but completely — organize by the 9 points above, with file:line references, and explicitly flag anything that suggests the release branch concept is unused/aspirational vs. anything that suggests it's load-bearing (CI actually branches on it, deploy actually depends on it, etc).

2	
3	**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.
4	
5	See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.
6	
7	## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)
8	
9	To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
10	- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
11	- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
12	- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.
13	
14	## Release Branch Behaviour
15	
16	When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.
17	
18	**Before writing any code, always:**
19	1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
20	2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
21	3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.
22	
23	**Allowed on release branches:**
24	- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
25	- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
26	- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch
27	
28	**Not allowed on release branches:**
29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
30	- Refactoring
31	- Dependency changes
32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
33	
34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
35	
36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
37	
38	```bash
39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
42	
43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
45	```
46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

7	## Pre-Build Decisions

9	These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

20	### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
21	
22	**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
23	**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.
24	
25	### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
26	
27	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
28	**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.
29	
30	### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
31	
32	**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
33	**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
34	**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
35	**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
36	**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
37	**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.

110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111	
112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

114	## Overrides Pattern
115	
116	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
117	
118	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
119	
120	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
121	
122	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
123	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
124	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
125	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

160	## Contentful Content Type Management
161	
162	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.
163	
164	**Key paths:**
165	
166	- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
167	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)
168	
169	**To register a new content type:**
170	
171	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
172	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
173	
174	**To run the sync:**
175	
176	```
177	npm run sync:contentful
178	```
179	
180	Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account — in `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold it, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running the sync). Get the token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
181	
182	The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).
183	
184	**Relationship to the React component:**
185	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
186	
187	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

204	## Integration Map
205	
206	All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.
207	
208	**Boundary key:**
209	
210	- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
211	- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
212	- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
213	- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
214	- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
215	- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
216	- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

249	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
250	
251	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

253	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
254	
255	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

257	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
258	
259	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
260	
261	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
262	
263	```ts
264	import { Pool } from 'undici';
265	
266	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
267	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
268	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
269	  timeout: 8000,
270	});
271	
272	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
273	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
274	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
275	    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
276	  });
277	}
278	```

# Environment Strategy, Branching & SIT Pipeline — Claude Code Briefing

## Programme Context

Zimmermann is migrating from Magento 2 to Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) using the PWA Kit
(`template-retail-react-app`) as the storefront baseline, deployed on Managed Runtime (MRT).

Seven storefronts are in scope: AU, UK, US domestic, US international (Global-e), EU domestic,
EU international (Global-e), and ME. The Digital pipeline must support all six active SFCC
storefronts simultaneously. NewStore (OMS) runs a parallel SIT cycle on its own cadence and
converges with Digital only at the STAGE tier.

Zimmermann has 20 SFCC sandboxes available and no MRT environment licence restriction.
This enables a clean six-tier topology with no shared-environment contention.

169	- Represents production. Always deployable.
170	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR from `release/v*.*.*` only.

175	#### `release/v*.*.*`
176	- Naming convention: `release/v1.3.0`, `release/v1.3.1` etc.
177	- Branched from `develop` when a release window is scheduled.
178	- No new features merged here — bug fixes and release-prep only.

185	- Integration baseline. All feature branches merge here.

Here is the full evidence report, organized by your 9 points.

## 1. Git history — has `release/*`/`hotfix/*` ever existed?

**No `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branch has ever existed in this repo's history, local or remote.**

- `git branch -a` — only `develop`, `main`, several `feature/*`, `fix/*` branches exist (local + `origin/*`). No `release/` or `hotfix/` prefix anywhere.
- `git for-each-ref` (all refs including `refs/stash`) — same result, no release/hotfix refs.
- Confirmed live against GitHub directly via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches`: `['develop', 'feature/agent-docs-cleanup', 'feature/contentfulDoc', 'feature/docsUpdates', 'feature/fix-cd-release-core-data-import', 'feature/local-test-branch', 'fix/e2e-ci-timeout', 'main']` — no release/hotfix branch on the remote either.
- `gh pr list --base release --state all` → empty. No PR has ever targeted a `release` base branch.
- `git tag -l` → empty. No tags exist at all (contradicts the tag-naming convention documented in `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, which is itself only a proposal — see point 6).
- `git log --all --merges --oneline | grep -iE "release|hotfix"` → **zero matches**. No merge commit has ever referenced a release/hotfix branch.
- `git log --all --oneline --grep=release -i` returns 13 commits, but every one is a **commit message** using the word "release" in a docs/CI/rules context (e.g. `2c682b9 fix(rules): restore release/hotfix branch check in session-start skill`), not an actual release-branch operation. Verified via `git show 2c682b9`: the diff only touches `.claude/registry/*.md`, `.cursor/rules/skills/session-start.mdc` — pure documentation/rules editing, no branch was created or merged.
- Repo is young: first commit `cd60b7a` on 2026-06-12, most recent `51c0290` on 2026-07-31, 259 total commits — i.e., roughly 7 weeks old, still in "Detailed Design" phase (`.docs/memory/projectState.md:8`) with no production build yet. There has never been a release event to exercise the policy against.

**Verdict-relevant fact:** the branch-type has zero exercised history — it is 100% unexercised as of today.

## 2. `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`

Read in full (47 lines). It is a **complete, self-contained policy document**, not a stub:

- `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md:3` — scoping: applies only when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*`/`hotfix/*`; ignorable on `feature/*`/`fix/*`.
- `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md:7-12` — GitFlow back-merge rules: `release/*`→`main` must also back-merge to `develop`; `hotfix/*`→`main` must also back-merge to `develop`; `fix/release-*` back-merges are folded into the release back-merge (no separate PR).
- `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md:14-32` — "Release Branch Behaviour": mandatory plan-first + blast-radius assessment + explicit developer confirmation before any edit; allow-list (read-only skills, trivial copy/version-bump/flag-toggle changes, `fix/release-*` sub-branch for code fixes) vs. deny-list (new features, refactors, dependency changes, Tier 1/2 changes without owner approval).
- `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md:34-46` — concrete worked example with real git/gh commands (`git checkout release/v0.1.0`, `git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-...`, `gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 ...`), explicitly says "The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (**when CI lands**)" — note the parenthetical hedge, written as if the SIT gate wasn't live yet at authoring time (though `digital-sit.yml` now exists and is keyed on `release/**`, see point 3).

This document is fully fleshed out in tone and detail (not a placeholder), but it is written entirely in the hypothetical/prescriptive ("when on a release branch, do X") — nothing in it references a concrete instance.

## 3. CI/CD workflows — `.github/workflows/` (all 11 files read)

Several workflows have **real, non-trivial conditional logic keyed on `release/**`** — this is load-bearing, not decorative:

- **`digital-sit.yml`** ("SIT Gate") — triggers `on: push/pull_request: branches: ['release/**']` (`.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml:4-9`). Entire workflow (Playwright P0, Lighthouse CI, contract tests, bundle-size, `sit-gate` aggregation) only runs on `release/**` push/PR — never on `develop` or `feature/*`.
- **`deploy-sit.yml`** — triggers via `workflow_run` on the "SIT Gate" workflow, scoped `branches: ['release/**']` (`.github/workflows/deploy-sit.yml:4-9`). Deploy-to-SIT is entirely dependent on a `release/**` branch existing and passing its gate.
- **`qa.yml`** — `on.pull_request.branches` includes `develop` and `'release/**'` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml:5-7`). Multiple jobs have explicit branch-conditional behavior:
  - `.github/workflows/qa.yml:125`: `if [[ "${{ github.base_ref }}" == release/* ]]; then echo "e2e_scope=full"` — forces full E2E scope (bypassing per-story change-detection) only for `release/**`-targeted PRs.
  - `.github/workflows/qa.yml:436`: `e2e-browserstack` job only runs when `contains(github.base_ref, 'release/') || jira_keys != ''` — BrowserStack cross-browser suite is otherwise gated to release PRs (or Jira-tagged develop PRs).
  - `.github/workflows/qa.yml:451-460`: on `release/*` base, runs the **full** `e2e/tests/zimm` BrowserStack suite unscoped; elsewhere, greps to the PR's Jira key(s) only. Comment at `qa.yml:415-418` explains why: "a release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply."
- **`protected-file-guard.yml`** — `on.pull_request.branches` includes `develop`, `main`, `'release/**'` (`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml:9-12`); its `branch-target-guard` job references the flow "`feature/* → develop → (release/*) → main`" in its failure message (`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml:173`).
- **`weekly-agents.yml`** — `changelog-reminder` job (`.github/workflows/weekly-agents.yml:255-297`) runs `gh pr list --base "release"` weekly and posts a `/generate-changelog` reminder comment on any open PR targeting a release branch missing a changelog comment.
- **`deploy-dev.yml`** — triggers on `push: branches: [develop]` only (`.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml:3-6`); no release-branch logic. Straight branch→env mapping.
- **`deploy-test.yml`, `deploy-uat.yml`, `deploy-stg.yml`, `deploy-prod.yml`** — all four are **`workflow_dispatch`-only** (manual trigger) with a `ref` input (`deploy-test.yml:4-9`, `deploy-uat.yml:4-9`, `deploy-stg.yml:4-9`, `deploy-prod.yml:4-9`). None of them auto-trigger on any branch push. Their `ref` input defaults/examples mention `release/1.2.0` as an *example value a human could type in* (`deploy-stg.yml:7-9`, `deploy-uat.yml:7-9`, `deploy-test.yml:7-9`) — but nothing enforces that the ref actually be a release branch; a tag, `main`, `develop`, or any arbitrary branch/SHA works identically. This is a documentation hint in a UI label, not branch-keyed logic.
- **`upstream-release-watch.yml`** — "release" here refers to upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` GitHub releases, unrelated to this repo's `release/*` branch concept (`.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml:1-99`).

**Summary for point 3:** `digital-sit.yml`, `deploy-sit.yml`, `qa.yml`, and `protected-file-guard.yml` have genuinely load-bearing branch-pattern matching on `release/**` — these are not cosmetic. However, since no `release/*` branch has ever existed (point 1), **none of this logic has ever actually fired in a real run** — it is written, wired, and presumably never triggered. `.browserstack.yml` itself has no branch-scoping (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.browserstack.yml` — checked in full, no release reference); the release-vs-develop BrowserStack scoping decision lives entirely in `qa.yml`'s bash conditionals, not in the BrowserStack config file.

Staging vs. production deploys are **not** branch-triggered at all — they're `workflow_dispatch` (manual) with a free-text `ref`, and the only tier with a genuine automatic branch-based trigger is Dev (`push` to `develop`). SIT is the only tier whose deploy is chained off a `release/**`-scoped workflow (`deploy-sit.yml`'s `workflow_run` filter).

## 4. Managed Runtime deploy model

- `package.json:43,76-81` — `push` scripts: `"push": "npm run build && pwa-kit-dev push"`, and per-tier variants `push:dev|test|sit|staging|uat|prod` — all of the form `npm run build && pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`. The `-t <target>` flag is a **bundle-push to a named MRT environment**, not a branch reference. `pwa-kit-dev push` bundles whatever is currently checked out and pushes it to that MRT target/environment — it has no concept of "branch" at the tool level; branch-vs-target association exists only in whichever CI workflow happens to invoke it (or a developer's local checkout).
- **`mobify.config.js` does not exist in the repository** — I confirmed this with `find`/`ls` at repo root; no such file. Yet it is referenced as authoritative in two places: `.docs/architecture.md:108` ("MRT targets in `mobify.config.js` map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`") and `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:55` (listed as a Tier-1 frozen file alongside `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`). `.docs/memory/projectState.md:24` also flags `mobify.config.js` `sit` env entry as a still-**pending** item. This is a genuine artifact/doc mismatch, independent of the release-branch question, but relevant to "how thoroughly is deploy tooling actually built out" — a file the docs treat as load-bearing/frozen doesn't exist yet.
- `config/` directory (`config/default.js`, `dev.js`, `production.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `test.js`, `uat.js`, `sites.js`, `sites.generated.js`, `sites.overlay.js`, `utils.js`) holds the actual per-tier runtime config that `pwa-kit-runtime`'s `getConfig()` resolves via the `DEPLOY_TARGET` env var (per `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `DEPLOY_TARGET_MAP`), not by branch name.
- **Deployment model is bundle/manual-dispatch-based, not branch-based**, except for Dev (auto on `push` to `develop`, `deploy-dev.yml:3-6`) and SIT (auto via `workflow_run` chained off a `release/**` push/PR that passed `SIT Gate`). Test/UAT/Staging/Prod are all `workflow_dispatch` with a free-text `ref` — a human (or automation) can push any commit/tag/branch to any of those tiers at will; nothing in the tooling requires a long-lived `release/*` branch to exist for MRT promotion to work mechanically.
- This is corroborated explicitly by the team's own internal proposal — see point 6 — which argues MRT's tag/bundle model makes a long-lived branch unnecessary for anything past Dev.

## 5. `.docs/architecture.md`

Read in full (291 lines). Branching/CI/release content:

**Short answer for the Scrum Master: no, it hasn't been set up.** No `release/*` branch exists anywhere — not locally, not on GitHub, no tags, no PR has ever targeted one. Here's the full picture:

**What's confirmed missing**
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches` shows only `develop`, `main`, and a handful of `feature/*`/`fix/*` branches — no `release/*`, no `hotfix/*`.
- `git tag -l` is empty — no tags at all, despite AGENTS.md/Confluence describing a `v0.1.0`-style tagging scheme.
- The GitHub setup checklist (Confluence *7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist*, owned by Integration Lead) still lists **"Configure `release/**` branch protection"** as an open (⬜) task — it was never actually turned on in GitHub settings.
- `mobify.config.js` — the file AGENTS.md/architecture.md describe as mapping MRT targets (dev/sit/uat/stage/production) — doesn't exist in the repo yet either.

**What *is* built, waiting for it**
The CI pipeline is already wired to key off `release/**` — this part is real, not aspirational: `digital-sit.yml` (the full SIT quality gate) triggers on push/PR to `release/**`, `deploy-sit.yml` auto-deploys to SIT once that gate passes, and `qa.yml` runs the full BrowserStack cross-browser suite only on PRs targeting `release/**`. None of that has ever fired, because the branch it's watching for has never existed.

**Why it hasn't happened yet**
The project is ~7 weeks in, still in the Platform Setup / Sprint 1 phase (SFCC-1 epic is still "In Progress"). A release branch only gets cut at the end of a sprint when there's something ready to promote toward STAGE/UAT — that point hasn't been reached yet, so there's been nothing to create one for.

**One thing worth flagging before it does get created**: there's a draft, unapproved Confluence proposal ("Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion") that would change *how* the release branch gets used — instead of environments deploying "whatever's currently on `release/v0.1.0`," each environment would deploy an immutable tag cut from that branch, so Test/SIT/UAT can run independent cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. You (Marcel) already left review comments on it — SIT's trigger doesn't actually match tag-based promotion yet, the tag-permission model needs fixing, and `scripts/tagRelease.sh` conflicts with the new tagging approach. `.docs/memory/projectState.md` explicitly says not to implement this without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off. Worth resolving *before* the first release branch is cut, since it changes the SIT deploy mechanism itself.

**Suggested reply to the SM:** "Not yet — no release branch has been created, and its GitHub branch protection hasn't been configured either. The CI/CD pipeline is already built to support it (SIT gate + cross-browser tests trigger off it), but we haven't hit a sprint-end/promotion point yet. There's also an open decision on exactly how it'll be used (branch-based vs. tag-based promotion) that should get resolved before we cut the first one."

direct-branch-deploy model is final.

## Does zimmermann-pwa need a `release/*` branch?

**Yes — structurally, the current design requires something shaped like it. But it's never been exercised, and there's an open, unresolved proposal to change what a "release branch" actually deploys.** Full breakdown below.

### 1. Codebase: designed-in, but zero exercised history

- **No `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branch has ever existed** — confirmed via local git, `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches`, `git tag -l` (empty), `gh pr list --base release` (empty). The repo is ~7 weeks old (259 commits since 2026-06-12); no sprint has reached a promotion point yet.
- **But the CI wiring is real, not decorative.** `digital-sit.yml` (Playwright P0, Lighthouse CI, contract tests, bundle-size, aggregated as the "SIT Gate") triggers on push/PR to `release/**` — never on `develop` or `feature/*`. `deploy-sit.yml` auto-deploys to SIT via `workflow_run` chained off that gate passing. `qa.yml` runs the full, unscoped BrowserStack cross-browser suite only on PRs targeting `release/**` (vs. per-Jira-story-scoped E2E on `develop`). `protected-file-guard.yml` and the changelog-reminder in `weekly-agents.yml` also branch on it. This is genuine conditional logic sitting idle, waiting for a branch that's never been created.
- **Deployment itself doesn't mechanically require a branch.** `npm run push:*` is `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>` — a bundle push to a named MRT environment, with no concept of "branch" at the tool level. Test/UAT/Staging/Prod deploy workflows are all `workflow_dispatch`-only with a free-text `ref` input; only **Dev** auto-deploys off a branch push (`develop`), and **SIT** is the only tier whose deploy is *chained* off `release/**`-scoped CI. So above Dev, nothing in the deploy tooling itself demands a long-lived branch — only the SIT gate's trigger does.
- Supporting gaps: `package.json` is still `0.0.1`, no tags exist despite a documented tagging scheme, `mobify.config.js` (the file docs call the authoritative MRT-target map) doesn't exist yet, and two "Status — done" seed-prompt docs in `.docs/prompts/` overstate what was actually built (they reference a `docs/` tree that was never created).

### 2. Confluence: a live policy, and a competing draft that hasn't been decided

- The **Branching Guide (GitFlow)** and **Environment Topology & Promotion Path** pages are the current, adopted policy — `release/**` is described as a direct deployment target: STAGE and UAT are manually promoted from `release/v*.*.*`, and it's the required-status-check boundary (`Digital SIT Gate`) before anything moves past Dev/SIT.
- But the **"Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)"** page (draft, explicitly "for review by squad leads + Integration lead before this replaces anything in AGENTS.md") argues that model has two real problems: PR branches get deleted on merge to `develop` so there's nothing left to redeploy from later, and pointing Test/SIT/UAT all at "whatever's on `release/v0.1.0` right now" forces them into lockstep instead of independent test cycles. Its fix keeps cutting a `release/vX.Y.Z` branch every sprint — it just changes what environments deploy *from*: an immutable tag cut off that branch, not the branch's moving HEAD.
- **You (Marcel) already reviewed this proposal** and left unresolved findings in-thread: the tag-permission model needs two GitHub Rulesets, not one; SIT's real trigger (`workflow_run` off the gate) doesn't match what the proposal's flow diagram assumes is tag-based; `scripts/tagRelease.sh` (what the *current* guide prescribes) conflicts with the proposed `npm version` flow and is unaddressed; and the proposal's environment names don't match live GitHub environments. Those are still open.
- The **7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist** confirms `release/**` branch protection was never actually turned on in GitHub (still ⬜), and several MRT-adjacent items (MRT project slug, `mobify.config.js`) are also still open.

### 3. JIRA: no formal decision either way

- **SFCC-1 "Platform Setup & Environments"** (the epic covering CI/CD pipeline setup) is still **In Progress** — consistent with "nothing has shipped yet, so nothing has forced the release-branch question."
- The **2.4 Decision Log** has no entry for branching/release strategy — this was never formally decided as a DC-numbered item, it just exists as inherited policy text in AGENTS.md/Confluence from project setup.
- No Jira ticket tracks the tag-based-promotion proposal specifically — it lives only as a Confluence draft + your review comments + a note in `.docs/memory/projectState.md` ("do not implement without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal").

### Bottom line

The branch type is **architecturally load-bearing for one specific job**: it's the thing that scopes the expensive gates (full SIT gate, unscoped cross-browser BrowserStack) away from every `develop` PR, and it's the boundary that `fix/release-*` stabilization work lands on before STAGE/UAT/Prod. That job doesn't go away under either model on the table. What's genuinely open is *how* environments consume it — moving-branch-ref (current, documented, unconfigured) vs. immutable-tag-cut-from-the-branch (proposed, drafted, reviewed, not approved) — and that choice should be settled **before** the first real `release/*` branch gets cut, not discovered mid-cut, since it changes SIT's deploy trigger mechanically.

**Practical next step:** since Sprint 1 (SFCC-1) is still in progress, there's no urgency to cut one today — but the tag-based proposal's three open questions (Test-gate design, Test-gate scope, and SIT tag-triggering) should get a decision from squad leads + Integration Lead before the first sprint-end release, so the first cut doesn't have to be redone under a different promotion model a sprint later.

**Bottom line: not needed yet, but will be once Sprint 1 wraps — and the exact mechanism isn't settled.**

- No `release/*` branch exists today, and nothing requires one yet — SFCC-1 (Platform Setup) is still in progress, nothing has shipped, and Dev/SIT are already handled by branch/CI logic that doesn't need it.
- The CI pipeline (SIT gate, cross-browser BrowserStack) is already wired to fire on `release/**` the moment one appears — so creating it later is just "cut the branch," not "build the plumbing."
- Before cutting the first one, get squad leads + Integration Lead to close out the draft tag-based-promotion proposal (your own review comments on it are still open). Otherwise the first release branch gets built under the old direct-branch-deploy model and has to be redone once that proposal lands.

For the Scrum Master specifically: **no, it hasn't been set up — and that's expected at this stage, not a gap.**

Now I'm turning to the actual question about where the release branch fits in the project's GitFlow lifecycle. The release branch sits between develop and main — it's created at sprint boundaries once develop is stable and ready to promote, serving as the staging point before merging to production on main, while feature and fix branches feed into develop, and hotfix branches branch off main for urgent production fixes. Hotfix branches operate as a separate emergency path, branching directly from main and merging back to both main and develop to bypass the release cycle entirely. content.text:
It sits at the **sprint-boundary/stabilization stage — between `develop` and `main`**, not in the day-to-day flow:

```
feature/*, fix/*  ──┐
                     ├──▶ develop  (continuous integration — every merge auto-deploys to Dev, then SIT)
                     ┘         │
                                │  sprint ends, a batch of work is ready to promote
                                ▼
                        release/vX.Y.Z   ← cut from develop, once per sprint
                                │
                    fix/release-{v}-* ──┘ (stabilization-only fixes land here via PR,
                                            never new features)
                                │
                                ▼
                    Digital SIT Gate + full BrowserStack suite must pass
                                │
                    manual promotion: STAGE → UAT (business sign-off)
                                │
                                ▼
                              main   ← merge + tag, then back-merge to develop
```

`hotfix/*` is a separate emergency lane that skips this entirely — it branches straight from `main` and merges back to `main` + `develop`, bypassing `release/*` altogether (deadline-driven prod fixes shouldn't wait for a sprint boundary).

So in the lifecycle, `release/*` is the **last stop before production** — it's not a working branch like `feature/*`, it's a stabilization/promotion boundary that only gets created at sprint-end when something is actually ready to move past Dev/SIT. That's also exactly why none exists yet: Sprint 1 hasn't reached that boundary.

One caveat from the draft tag-based-promotion proposal still under review: it doesn't move `release/*` to a different spot in this lifecycle — it still gets cut from `develop` at sprint-end, same position. It only changes what STAGE/UAT/Prod actually deploy *from* (an immutable tag cut off the branch, not the branch's live HEAD).
